controls.label: Visible color
controls.notes: Visible-light appearance from the prepared OpenSpace Saturn mosaic. This is a presentation texture assembled from observations, not a live image of the scene date.

controls.label: Ultraviolet
controls.notes: Hubble OPAL F225W (225 nm), August 2025, shown in false color. Broad ultraviolet structure is measured; missing polar/ring-occluded rows are filled along longitude and fine detail comes from a bounded visible-light transfer. This composite is not pure ultraviolet imagery.

controls.label: Methane
controls.notes: Hubble OPAL FQ889N (889 nm), August 2025, shown in false color. This methane-absorption band traces atmospheric structure, not a methane concentration map. Missing rows and fine visible-light detail are filled as described for ultraviolet.

controls.label: Thermal illustration
controls.notes: Schematic illustration from visible-light morphology and authored patterns. Colors do not measure infrared brightness or temperature; this is not a Cassini observation.

controls.label: Cross section
controls.notes: Schematic interior layers based on models of Saturn. Boundaries, colors and exposed structure illustrate inferred composition; they are not photographs or a measured interior map.

charts.alt: Modeled disk reflectance of Saturn from 350 to 1000 nanometers, including the methane absorption band at 889 nanometers.
Saturn globe-only V-band brightness change across phase angles from zero to 150 degrees.
Saturn atmospheric temperature from 10 bar to 2 nanobar, showing the cold tropopause and warmer upper atmosphere.

charts.title: Saturn modeled disk reflectance
charts.description: Full 253-point NASA PSG spectrum from 350 to 1000 nanometers. The band marks ultraviolet, visible light and near-infrared wavelengths.

charts.title: Saturn temperature-pressure profile
charts.description: NASA PSG vertical atmosphere model from 10 bar to 2 nanobar. Pressure decreases upward on a logarithmic scale.

charts.title: Saturn photometric phase curve
charts.description: V-band dimming of Saturn as phase angle increases from zero to 150 degrees.

source.title: Computing Apparent Planetary Magnitudes for The Astronomical Almanac
source.qualification: V-band phase equations transcribed from equations 2 through 17. Distance, rotation, season, latitude, and ring terms cancel or are held fixed so each curve isolates phase-angle dependence.

metadata.qualification: Globe-only phase curve. The rings are excluded because no wide-angle combined planet-and-ring equation is available.
metadata.measurement: V-band magnitude change relative to zero-degree phase
